# Tracking the top clones over time {#sec-top-clones}

**What it shows.** For each patient, the share of every sample's repertoire held by the
patient's largest clones, followed from sample to sample. Clones are TCRβ clonotypes (CDR3β +
V gene), the unit the clonal dynamics test uses: a paired α/β clone splits whenever a cell loses
its α chain, so following the β chain keeps one clone together.

**Why it matters.** The clonal dynamics tables say *which* clones changed significantly; this
view shows *how much* of the repertoire they take up and *when*: a clone that dominates one
timepoint, a set of clones that rise together after treatment, or a repertoire that stays
diverse throughout.

**How to read it.** One tab per patient. Each bar is one sample, in timepoint order; the
numbered blocks at the bottom are the patient's largest clones (ranked by their peak share in
any of the patient's samples) and the grey block above is every other clone. Ribbons only join
consecutive samples of the same compartment; they are not measurements between them. The key
under the figure gives each clone's CDR3β, its peak share and whether the clonal dynamics
analysis called it expanding or contracting. Hover a block for its exact share.

```{r}
#| label: top-clones-tracking
#| results: asis
trk <- T("clonal", "clonotypes.csv")
trk_n <- max(1L, as.integer(params$top_n_tracked_clones %||% 6))
if (!have(trk) || !all(c("sample", "junction_aa") %in% names(trk))) {
  cat(as.character(note("The clonal dynamics clonotype table is missing, so clones cannot be tracked over time.")))
} else {
  pc <- intersect(c(as_str1(params$patient_col), "patient", "patient_id", "subject_id"), names(trk))[1]
  trk$patient_ <- if (is.na(pc)) "all" else as.character(trk[[pc]])
  trk$origin_  <- if ("origin" %in% names(trk)) as.character(trk$origin) else "all"
  trk$origin_[is.na(trk$origin_) | !nzchar(trk$origin_)] <- "all"
  trk$tp_      <- if ("timepoint" %in% names(trk)) as.character(trk$timepoint) else as.character(trk$sample)
  trk$alias_   <- if ("alias" %in% names(trk)) as.character(trk$alias) else as.character(trk$sample)
  trk$v_       <- if ("v_call" %in% names(trk)) sub("\\*.*$", "", as.character(trk$v_call)) else ""
  trk$key      <- paste(trk$junction_aa, trk$v_, sep = "|")
  if (!"frequency" %in% names(trk)) trk$frequency <- trk$duplicate_count / ave(trk$duplicate_count, trk$sample, FUN = sum)
  tpo <- trimws(strsplit(as_str1(params$timepoint_order), ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]); tpo <- tpo[nzchar(tpo)]
  trk$rank_ <- if ("timepoint_rank" %in% names(trk)) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(trk$timepoint_rank)) else NA
  miss <- is.na(trk$rank_); trk$rank_[miss] <- match(trk$tp_[miss], c(tpo, sort(setdiff(unique(trk$tp_), tpo))))

  fr_all <- trk %>% group_by(patient_, origin_, sample, key) %>%
    summarise(pct = 100 * sum(frequency), .groups = "drop")
  smp_all <- trk %>% distinct(patient_, origin_, sample, tp_, alias_, rank_) %>%
    distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% arrange(patient_, origin_, rank_, alias_)
  # Clones the clonal dynamics analysis called (patient x CDR3b), for the key.
  called <- function(f, lab) {
    t <- T("clonal", f)
    if (!have(t) || !"junction_aa" %in% names(t)) return(NULL)
    tpc <- intersect(c(as_str1(params$patient_col), "patient", "patient_id", "subject_id"), names(t))[1]
    data.frame(patient_ = if (is.na(tpc)) "all" else as.character(t[[tpc]]),
               junction_aa = as.character(t$junction_aa), call = lab)
  }
  calls <- bind_rows(called("expanded_clones_summary.csv", "expanding"),
                     called("contracting_clones_summary.csv", "contracting"))
  calls <- if (nrow(calls)) calls %>% distinct() %>% group_by(patient_, junction_aa) %>%
    summarise(call = paste(sort(unique(call)), collapse = " and "), .groups = "drop") else
    data.frame(patient_ = character(), junction_aa = character(), call = character())

  # A patient is tracked in every compartment it was sampled at least twice in.
  panels <- smp_all %>% count(patient_, origin_) %>% filter(n >= 2)
  pats <- sort(unique(panels$patient_))
  skipped <- setdiff(unique(smp_all$patient_), pats)
  if (!length(pats)) {
    cat(as.character(note("No patient was sampled at two or more timepoints in one compartment, so no clone can be tracked over time.")))
  } else {
    patient_tabs(pats, function(pt) {
      ors <- panels$origin_[panels$patient_ == pt]
      figs <- list(); keytxt <- character()
      for (o in ors) {
        smp <- smp_all %>% filter(patient_ == pt, origin_ == o)
        fr  <- fr_all %>% filter(patient_ == pt, origin_ == o)
        peak <- fr %>% group_by(key) %>% summarise(peak = max(pct), .groups = "drop") %>%
          arrange(desc(peak), key) %>% head(trk_n)
        keys <- peak$key
        cdr3 <- sub("\\|.*$", "", keys)
        cl <- calls$call[match(paste(pt, cdr3), paste(calls$patient_, calls$junction_aa))]
        cols <- setNames(as.list(track_slate[seq_along(keys)]), keys)
        lab  <- setNames(paste0(seq_along(keys), "  ", cdr3), keys)
        dup  <- duplicated(smp$tp_) | duplicated(smp$tp_, fromLast = TRUE)
        smp$label <- ifelse(dup, smp$alias_, smp$tp_)
        smp$hover <- paste0(smp$alias_, " (", smp$tp_, ")")
        ttl_ <- if (length(ors) > 1) paste0(pt, " · ", o, ": top ", length(keys), " clones") else
          paste0(pt, ": top ", length(keys), " clones")
        figs[[o]] <- track_plot(fr, smp, keys, cols, lab, ttl_, unit = "TCRβ clonotype counts")
        keytxt <- c(keytxt, paste0(if (length(ors) > 1) paste0("<em>", htmltools::htmlEscape(o), ":</em> ") else "",
          clone_key_html(keys, cdr3, paste0("peak ", sprintf("%.1f%%", peak$peak),
                                            ifelse(is.na(cl), "", paste0(" · called ", cl))), cols)))
      }
      htmltools::tagList(
        figcap(htmltools::tagList(figs), "T1", "Top clones over time",
               paste("Share of each sample's repertoire held by the patient's largest TCRβ clonotypes",
                     "(numbered by peak share; grey = all other clones). Bars are samples in timepoint",
                     "order; ribbons only join consecutive samples. The share is of the sample's",
                     "receptor counts: cells on single-cell routes, templates or reads on bulk routes.")),
        htmltools::tags$div(style = "font-size:0.88rem;margin:0.2rem 0 1rem 0;",
                            htmltools::HTML(paste(keytxt, collapse = "<br>"))))
    })
    if (length(skipped)) cat(sprintf("\n*Not shown (fewer than two samples in any compartment): %s.*\n\n",
                                     paste(sort(skipped), collapse = ", ")))
  }
}
```

# Consensus clustering {#sec-consensus}

**What it is.** Receptors that recognise the same epitope tend to be similar rather than
identical, and each clustering method captures similarity differently: GIANA (CDR3β geometry
plus V gene), GLIPH2 (shared CDR3β motifs) and TCRdist3 (biochemical distance over the CDR
loops), all per patient; on the single-cell VDJ+GEX route also CoNGA, whose hit clonotypes are
grouped by their gene-expression and TCR clusters. Two clonotypes are linked when at least
`--consensus_min_methods` methods (default 2) put them in the same cluster, and each connected
group is one consensus cluster.

**Receptor-only and receptor + expression methods.** CoNGA is the only method that uses both
the receptor (VDJ) and the cell's gene expression (GEX); GIANA, GLIPH2 and TCRdist3 use the
receptor sequence alone, and CoNGA only runs on the VDJ+GEX route. This helps interpret a
cluster by which methods support it:

- **Supported by the receptor-only methods alone**: the receptors are similar, a sequence-level
  prediction of shared specificity, whatever the cells' phenotype.
- **Supported by CoNGA as well**: the similar receptors also sit in cells with the same
  transcriptional programme. Two independent kinds of evidence agree, which makes a shared
  antigen-driven response much more likely; these are the strongest candidates.
- **Supported by CoNGA and only one receptor method**: the expression signal may be carrying
  the cluster; check whether it is an innate-like population (MAIT, iNKT), whose semi-invariant
  receptors cluster with a fixed phenotype without sharing a conventional antigen.

On the bulk and VDJ-only routes, consensus rests on receptor similarity only.

**Why it matters.** A cluster that independent definitions of similarity agree on is far less
likely to be an artefact of one method, so consensus clusters are the strongest candidates for
groups of receptors sharing a specificity, to test against known epitopes or follow over time.

**How to read it.** The bar chart ranks the largest consensus clusters by cells (clonotype rows
for bulk data); the table gives each cluster's patient, the methods that support it and the
cluster each method gave it. Clusters spanning several clonotypes and supported by three or
more methods are the most robust. Each method's own results are in the **Details: Patient**
report, and on the VDJ+GEX route the cell states of these clusters are in the GEX section below.

```{r}
#| label: consensus
if (!have(cons_clusters)) {
  note("Consensus clustering produced no clusters on this run.")
} else {
  save_table(cons_clusters, "master_consensus_clusters.tsv")
  d <- cons_clusters
  nc <- intersect(c("n_cells", "cells", "n"), names(d))
  cc <- intersect(c("consensus_cluster", "cluster"), names(d))
  if (!length(nc) || !length(cc)) itable(d, pageSize = 15) else {
    dd <- data.frame(cat = as.character(d[[cc[1]]]), val = as.numeric(d[[nc[1]]]))
    dd <- dd[order(-dd$val), , drop = FALSE]
    dd <- head(dd, params$top_n_clusters)
    dd$hover <- paste0("cluster ", dd$cat, "<br>", dd$val, " cells")
    hbar(dd, paste0("Top ", params$top_n_clusters, " consensus clusters"), "Cells", height = 560)
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: consensus-table
itable(cons_clusters, pageSize = 10)
```

# Reference tables

Every figure in this report is a view of one of the run's core tables, written to
`results/` by RESULTS_EXPORT whether or not the reports render: `samples.tsv`,
`clones.tsv.gz`, `clone_tests.tsv.gz`, `sample_overlap.tsv` and, with single-cell data,
`cells.tsv.gz` and `marker_expression.tsv`. `results/README.md` lists their columns and the
table behind each figure. With `--write_figure_tables true` each figure's own data is also
written to `Master_Summary_Report/tables/`.

```{r}
#| label: written-tables
files <- list.files(file.path(params$outdir, "tables"), pattern = "\\.tsv$")
if (length(files)) itable(data.frame(table = sort(files), stringsAsFactors = FALSE), pageSize = 25)
```
